rows.question: When is a Singapore GST return due after each quarter?
rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

#### IRAS — GST

**Status:** Verified evidence; case application unresolved

**GST return filing deadline, nil-return duty, and extension procedure** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** A GST return and any tax due are generally due one month after the accounting period ends. A nil return is still required when there was no business activity. For GIRO, deduction is on the 15th of the month after the payment due date, shifted to the next working day if it falls on a weekend or public holiday. [GST Filing Due Dates and Requests for Extension | Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/filing-gst/gst-filing-due-dates-and-requests-for-extension)

**Source:** GST Filing Due Dates and Requests for Extension | Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST return filing deadline, nil-return duty, and extension procedure): You must file a “Nil” return even if you had no business activity during the accounting period.

Filing and payment due dates

Your GST return and payment are due 1 month after the end of your accounting period. If you pay via GIRO, IRAS will deduct payment on the 15th day of the month after the payment due date. If the deduction date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deduction will be made on the next working day.

Without GIRO

GST Accounting Period  | File and pay by

Jan - Mar  | 30 Apr

Apr - Jun  | 31 Jul

Jul - Sept  | 31 Oct

Oct - Dec  | 31 Jan

With GIRO

GST Accounting Period  | File by | GIRO deduction Date

Jan - Mar  | 30 Apr  | 15 May

Apr - Jun  | 31 Jul  | 15 Aug

Jul - Sept  | 31 Oct  | 15 Nov

Oct - Dec  | 31 Jan  | 15 Feb

Note: To confirm that your GST will be paid via GIRO, check the acknowledgement page after you file your GST F5 return.
- Official source: [GST Filing Due Dates and Requests for Extension | Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/filing-gst/gst-filing-due-dates-and-requests-for-extension)

Restructuring of company  | e.g. Notice of restructuring, media release  | 2 weeks

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Employee and employer CPF contribution rate factors** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** CPF contribution rates depend on citizenship or permanent-resident status (including the applicable PR year), age group, and total wages or wage band. Use the rate table effective for the contribution period being assessed. For employees in their first two years of permanent-resident status, the employer and employee may jointly apply for a higher contribution rate under CPF’s options. This is a general explanation and does not determine an employee’s rate or calculate contributions. [How Much CPF Contributions to Pay | Central Provident Fund Board (CPF Board) (offline fixture title)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay)

**Source:** How Much CPF Contributions to Pay | Central Provident Fund Board (CPF Board) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Employee and employer CPF contribution rate factors): CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee's citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
Here’s how to determine the year of SPR status:
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
View an example
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1 (PDF, 0.2MB))
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5 (PDF, 0.2MB))
Learn more
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Age group
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
View an example
Wage band
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
- Official source: [How Much CPF Contributions to Pay | Central Provident Fund Board (CPF Board) (offline fixture title)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay)

- **CPF rule explanation:** CPF contribution rates depend on citizenship or permanent-resident status (including the applicable PR year), age group, and total wages or wage band. - **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Employee and employer CPF contribution rate factors): CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee's citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
Here’s how to determine the year of SPR status:
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
View an example
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1 (PDF, 0.2MB))
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5 (PDF, 0.2MB))
Learn more
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Age group
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
View an example
Wage band
Different rates apply for different wage bands.

rows.question: When is final salary due if an employee serves the full notice period?
rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Ministry of Manpower — Employment requirements

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Final salary deadline when an employee resigns with required notice** (party in scope: Employee)
- **MOM rule explanation:** MOM distinguishes final wages by how employment ends: where an employee serves required resignation notice, pay on the last day of employment; resignation without notice, within 7 days of the last day of employment; misconduct dismissal, on the last day of employment or within 3 working days from dismissal if that is not possible; and employer termination, on the last day of employment or within 3 working days from termination if that is not possible. The rule is for employees covered by the Employment Act. Determine which of the four termination paths applies; resignation with notice and without notice have different deadlines. Foreign employees leaving employment have a separate tax clearance withholding requirement, which may withhold salary and leave pay for up to 30 days after the cessation notice to the Comptroller. Commission-payment timing may depend on contract, policies or practices. The current page does not establish historical applicability. A case-specific conclusion requires: Employment Act coverage and whether employee resigned with notice, resigned without notice, was dismissed for misconduct, or was terminated by the employer. Last employment day or termination/dismissal date. Any foreign-employee tax-clearance notice and contract-specific commission terms. General rule summary; does not decide a dispute about notice validity, breach, misconduct, wrongful dismissal or amounts owed. Tax-clearance withholding is a separate issue and depends on the foreign employee and cessation-notice facts. [Paying Salary | Ministry of Manpower (MOM) (offline fixture title)](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

**Source:** Paying Salary | Ministry of Manpower (MOM) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Final salary deadline when an employee resigns with required notice): If you are covered by the Employment Act, your employer must pay your salary at least once a month.

They can also pay it at shorter intervals if they choose.

Salary must be paid:

• Within 7 days after the end of the salary period

• For overtime work, within 14 days after the end of the salary period

Your final salary payment could vary depending on the following situations:

In this situation | Your final salary must be paid

Employee resigns and serves the required notice period | On the last day of employment.

Employee resigns and does not serve the notice period | Within 7 days of the last day of employment.

Dismissal on grounds of misconduct

On the last day of employment.

If this is not possible, then within 3 working days from date of dismissal.

Employer terminates the contract

On the last day of employment.

If this is not possible, then within 3 working days from date of termination.

• If your contract involves commission, how and when the commission is paid depends on what is in your employment contract or existing policies or practices.

• If you’re a foreign employee who is leaving your employment, your employer is required to withhold all your monies due to you for tax clearance for up to 30 days upon giving notice of the cessation of your employment to the Comptroller of Income Tax. The monies include your salary, leave pay, etc.
- Official source: [Paying Salary | Ministry of Manpower (MOM) (offline fixture title)](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

**Private-company small-company audit exemption criteria** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** Small-company audit exemption requires the entity to be a private company in the financial year and to meet at least two of the three quantitative criteria for each of the immediate past two consecutive financial years: revenue no more than S$10 million, assets no more than S$10 million, or no more than 50 full-time employees at FYE. A company that is less than two years old is assessed against criteria in its current year. A group also has to meet the separate consolidated small-group criteria. Two of three criteria must hold for both immediately preceding consecutive financial years for an established company; “this year and last year” does not always establish that period. The Singapore company and the entire group (including foreign entities) must each satisfy their respective test where the company is part of a group. A qualifying company remains qualified until it ceases to be private or no longer meets at least two criteria over the immediate past two consecutive financial years. The current-year test applies to a newly incorporated private company less than two years old. A separate dormant-company audit exemption may apply; do not confuse audit exemption with relief from preparing financial statements or filing an annual return. A case-specific conclusion requires: Private-company status during the financial year. Revenue, total assets and full-time employee count for the immediate past two consecutive financial years. If part of a group, the consolidated figures and entire-group scope. Whether the company is newly incorporated or another audit exception is being considered. A company-specific conclusion needs two financial years’ facts and, for a group, consolidated facts. Audit exemption does not exempt a company from keeping proper records, preparing financial statements, annual-return filing or tax filing. Who qualifies for audit exemption
To qualify for audit exemption as a small company, you need to meet both of these criteria:
Your company is a private company in the financial year; and
Your company meets at least two of these quantitative criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years:
Total annual revenue of $10 million or less, based on your financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
Total assets of $10 million or less, based on your financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year
Detailed exemption criteria
If your company is newly incorporated (less than two years old)
You qualify for audit exemption if you meet the criteria in the current financial year.
Example:
First financial year: Check if you are a private company and meet two out of three quantitative criteria that year.
Second financial year: If you did not qualify in the first year, check again using the same requirements for the second year.
If your company is part of a group
You need to meet both of these conditions to qualify for audit exemption:
Your Singapore company or subsidiary qualifies as a small company; and
Your entire group (including foreign entities) meets at least two of these quantitative criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years:
Total annual revenue of $10 million or less, based on your holding company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
Total assets of $10 million or less, based on your holding company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year
Note: The audit exemption applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 July 2015.
Maintaining your exemption status
Once your company qualifies as a small company, you remain qualified in subsequent financial years unless:
You cease to be a private company at any time during a financial year; or
You do not meet at least two out of three criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years
Once your group qualifies as a small group, it remains qualified for subsequent financial years. This applies until it does not meet at least two out of three criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years.

Can companies with corporate shareholders get audit exemption?
Yes, you can qualify for audit exemption even if you have corporate shareholders.
Unlike the previous criteria, you do not need to be an exempt private company to qualify for audit exemption.
Does the small company criteria affect financial statement filing?
No, it does not change your financial statement filing requirements.

rows.question: What is MAS’s VCFM regime for venture capital fund managers?
rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence is incomplete for one or more material issues.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** Additional case facts or checks are required; see the issue-level limitations.
**Material evidence gaps:** See the evidence gaps and coverage limitations below.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Verified evidence; case application unresolved

**Simplified VCFM licensing path and admission eligibility** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** At a high level, MAS describes a VCFM as an LFMC that operates under a simplified VCFM regime. A company that solely manages venture capital funds may apply to use this route. MAS says VCFMs follow simplified admission criteria; the cited page points to Appendix 4 but does not give a full side-by-side comparison or its detailed criteria. The route requires an application and is not automatic eligibility. MAS also considers the business model and risks, risk and compliance controls, track record and expertise, fitness and propriety, minimum financial requirements, and dedicated secure office arrangements; check Appendix 4 before deciding whether a particular manager qualifies. [Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/capital-markets/apply-for-licensing-or-registration-of-capital-market-entities/fund-management-licensing)
- **Application unresolved:** For Simplified VCFM licensing path and admission eligibility, case-specific treatment or calculation has not been verified. The relevant facts and statutory conditions still need to be established.

**Source:** Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Simplified VCFM licensing path and admission eligibility): If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Verified evidence; case application unresolved

**Conditional class exemptions from fund-management licensing** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** A fund manager does not become exempt merely because it manages assets for a related corporation or family member. MAS says a company operating under an existing class exemption does not require a licence, and gives related-corporation or family assets, certain immovable-asset pools, and certain non-capital-markets-product pools for accredited or institutional investors as examples that may be eligible. The specific exemption conditions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Regulations must be checked before concluding that a particular manager is exempt. [Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/capital-markets/apply-for-licensing-or-registration-of-capital-market-entities/fund-management-licensing)

- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Conditional class exemptions from fund-management licensing): If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations.
